name: IGVH MUTATION BY NGS
interpretation:
• A productive IGHV3-30*04 or IGHV3-30-3*03/IGHD3-9*01/IGHJ6*02 gene was detected.

  • The rearranged IGHV gene had 99.31% nucleotide identity with the germline sequence of the IGHV3-30*01 gene.

  • Following the 98% germline identity cut-off value which is used for discriminating CLL cases into the IG-mutated or IG-unmutated category, this case belongs to; 

IG-unmutated category which is generally associated with adverse prognosis.

CLINICAL BACKGROUND:

  • B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most frequent form of leukemia in adults which is characterized by a progressive accumulation of functionally incompetent B-cells.
  • IGHV mutation status is used as a CLL prognostic markers.

Unmutated IGHV

  • Defined as <2% difference from the germline VH gene sequence identity
  • Poor prognosis: Aggressive disease course, relatively shorter overall survival
  • 40% of CLL cases are unmutated IGHV

Mutated IGHV HV-M

  • Defined as >2% difference from the germline VH gene sequence identity
  • Good prognosis: Longer overall survival

METHODOLOGY:

  • PCR amplification of IGHV-IGHD-IGHJ gene rearrangements with FR1 primers.
  • Next generation sequencing
  • Immunoinformatics analysis: IMGT V-Quest
  • VH FR1 primers might underestimate the total number of IGHV somatic hypermutations as a part of the VH domain is missing.
  • The above report has been generated in accordance with the latest ERIC recommendations for Immunoglobulin gene sequence analysis in CLL.
